author: show-me state times
title: Justice Department announces $250,000 settlement in Springfield landlord sexual harassment case
text:
The Justice Department announced on Apr. 29 that the owners of residential rental properties in and around Springfield, Missouri have agreed to pay $250,000 to resolve a lawsuit alleging sexual harassment of female tenants by the properties’ former owner and manager in violation of the Fair Housing Act.
The case addresses concerns about tenant safety and landlord accountability under federal law. According to Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, “A home should be a place of safety, not fear and exploitation. The Justice Department is committed to vigorously holding landlords accountable when they use their power to violate the rights of vulnerable tenants.”
U.S. Attorney R. Matthew Price for the Western District of Missouri said, “No tenant should ever be forced to choose between their safety and keeping a roof over their head. Exploiting power for sexual coercion and retaliation is not only immoral, but it’s also illegal. The result of this case makes it clear that the Western District of Missouri will work tirelessly to hold accountable any landlord who violates a tenant’s rights.” Assistant Secretary for Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity Craig Trainor at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development added, “The Fair Housing Act protects against sex discrimination precisely to prohibit this kind of vile and predatory behavior against vulnerable women… The Trump Administration will always stand with victims and hold perpetrators accountable.” Special Agent in Charge Machelle Jindra with HUD’s Office of Inspector General said, “Today’s settlement makes clear that landlords who abuse their position… will be held accountable… we will continue to work with our partners to hold offenders fully responsible.”
The lawsuit was filed in March 2024 in U.S. District Court for the Western District of Missouri against Jimmie Bell—who died in February 2025—and other property owners or trustees after allegations spanning more than a decade involving unwanted sexual comments or advances toward female tenants as well as retaliatory evictions or refusal to make repairs when advances were refused.
Under terms outlined by authorities, defendants must pay compensation; remove retaliatory evictions from records; stop seeking payments from affected former tenants; and implement training at all relevant properties regarding discrimination prevention.
The U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri handles federal prosecutions and civil litigation across 66 counties according to its official website. Its jurisdiction stretches from Iowa’s border southward through Arkansas’s border, covering an area from Kansas eastward halfway across Missouri according to its official website. Offices are located in Kansas City, Jefferson City, and Springfield according to its official website. The office collaborates with federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement partners according to its official website while supporting outreach programs focused on issues like violent crime according to its official website, operating as part of the U.S. Department of Justice according to its official website.
This settlement forms part of an ongoing initiative launched by the department in October 2017 targeting sexual harassment by those controlling access or services related housing.
